summary.intent: Investigate GitHub issue #644 (five hardware verification gates for the FUSE-T/FSKit driver decision) and run the actual gate measurements needed to de-risk that decision before crates/fuse implementation begins.
summary.outcome: Built a standalone hw-gates harness, upgraded FUSE-T to 1.2.7, and ran gates 1-4 to completion (gates 1-3 pass with noattrcache required, gate 4 conditional on a commercial license); gate 5 recorded as blocked on macOS 27 beta hardware. Landed results, updated the blueprint, opened a draft PR, and ran /simplify to clean up the harness code before the pending /security-review.

repo: FUSE-T and macFUSE both register as 'fuse' in pkg-config on this machine, so an unqualified fuser build can silently link the wrong backend (macFUSE, which requires a kext) instead of FUSE-T (which doesn't).

The vendored/patched fuser (socket-read fragmentation patch, macOS rpath link-args) used in v1 no longer lives in the main tree's tools dir — only a stale Cargo.lock remains there; the actual patched source is on the frozen v1 branch.
crates/fuse is currently just a 20-line placeholder crate with no FileAttr/Filesystem impl and no fuser dependency — real FS projection is deferred to a later PR.
Sync timing profile constants live in crates/engine/src/profile.rs.

blueprint/desktop.md and blueprint/testing.md use a convention of full markdown links to cipher-box-next issues (e.g. cipher-box-next#47) rather than bare '#N', since bare refs would autolink to the wrong repo.
FUSE-T 1.2.7 ships as two pkg receipts, org.fuse-t.core and org.fuse-t.fskit (the fskit component is a new FSKit backend, but it doesn't support notifications, so it's not a shortcut for gate 5).
libfuse-t exports fuse_mount_compat25, so fuser should link the plain libfuse2-compatible path, not the macfuse-4-compat path.

code.finding: Patched to prefer fuse-t.pc via pkg-config over macFUSE's; later the FUSE-T rpath was moved here (into the fuse-t branch, computed from the probed libdir) rather than living as a hardcoded global rustflag.

child_for_rename's prefix-fallback path silently 'repairs' a failed exact-name lookup during rename, which could mask the exact truncation bug gate 3 is meant to detect; simplify pass changed a fallback hit to fail gate 3 instead of just being counted.
Store-mutation boilerplate (lock store, get_mut, mutate NodeKind::File, bump mtime) was duplicated ~9 times across gate1/gate1b/gate2; consolidated into a single edit() helper on Mounted.
read_first held-descriptor reader closure was duplicated verbatim between gate1 and gate1b; consolidated into one module-scope fn.
Measurement-loop scaffolding (Vec + timeout counter + poll_until match + stats_line) repeated ~9 times in gate1/gate1b; consolidated via a measure() helper.

Normative requirements (mount noattrcache; fire push invalidation on remote change) were interleaved with transient measurement provenance (p95 numbers, dated execution log); trimmed so RESULTS.md carries the transient data and the blueprint states only the durable requirement.

workflow: Run otool -L (or equivalent) on a freshly built binary before executing it when multiple libraries could satisfy the same linker name — this would have caught the macFUSE/FUSE-T mislink before it triggered a kext approval prompt.
When a user message arrives mid-turn, stop and answer it immediately rather than continuing tool calls and burying the reply — ignoring it even once is a serious trust break.
Background bash tasks and background agents both deliver a task-notification on completion; results can be picked up asynchronously without polling.
/simplify's 4 parallel review agents (reuse, simplification, efficiency, altitude) can each return 'clean' — not every review angle needs to produce findings.
Signed commits via 1Password SSH agent can silently stall if the agent app isn't unlocked; retrying the same commit command after unlock succeeds without other changes.

friction: A gate-harness binary accidentally linked against macFUSE instead of FUSE-T (both register as 'fuse' in pkg-config), triggering an unexpected macOS kernel-extension approval dialog for the user.

The assistant continued working through tool calls after this happened and effectively ignored two consecutive user messages asking about the dialog before addressing it, causing real user frustration ('the actual fuck').
Initial gate 1 harness runs failed to resolve lookups through the mount, requiring an ad hoc 'serve' debug mode and a background-held mount to diagnose.
Extended gate 1 run hit long 10s/30s timeouts on held-open-descriptor invalidation rounds, pushing it into the background and delaying results (though the timeout itself became a real finding).
1Password SSH commit signing failed to respond twice, blocking the commit until the user returned and unlocked it.

A build after the rpath refactor (moving from hardcoded rustflags to build.rs-emitted, pkg-config-derived rpath) initially produced no binary, requiring further investigation before it could be verified.
open_items: Gate 5 (FSKit spike) remains blocked on hardware — needs a macOS 27 beta machine or VM to exercise FSVolume.DataCacheHandler / FSClient.mountSingleVolume.
Gate 4 requires actually negotiating a commercial license from FUSE-T's author (alex@fuse-t.org) before bundling FUSE-T in the shipped app; no published pricing yet.
crates/fuse itself is still just a placeholder — the real FS projection (mounting with noattrcache, wiring push invalidation on every remote change) is deferred to a later PR.
/security-review is still pending on PR #736 as the next mandatory gate after /simplify (no crypto surface expected, so no separate crypto review needed).
A debug SMB mount and its background serve process were torn down mid-session but should be double-checked as fully cleaned up before considering the harness state final.
